triggers: compare two things with a diagram
template: A Venn diagram is the best way to show relationships. By placing {context} in the overlapping circles, you can easily see what they share and where they differ.
fallback: A Venn diagram uses overlapping circles to illustrate the logical relationships between two or more sets of items.

template: UML diagrams are standard for software design. If you are looking at {context}, a class diagram or sequence diagram would be the most effective choice to model it.
fallback: UML, or Unified Modeling Language, is a standardized way to visualize the design of a system, commonly used in software engineering.

template: For managing {context}, a Gantt chart is ideal. It provides a horizontal bar chart that tracks your schedule, milestones, and dependencies over time.
fallback: A Gantt chart is a type of bar chart that illustrates a project schedule, showing the start and finish dates of the various elements of a project.

template: A mind map is great for expanding on {context}. You start with that core idea in the center and branch out into related topics and sub-ideas organically.
fallback: Mind maps are radial diagrams used to visually organize information, typically starting with a single concept in the center and branching outward.

template: To get to the root of {context}, I'd suggest a Fishbone diagram. It helps you categorize potential causes of a problem to find the actual source.
fallback: A Fishbone (or Ishikawa) diagram is a visualization tool for categorizing the potential causes of a problem to identify its root source.

template: An ER diagram is the gold standard for database design. It would allow you to map out how {context} relates to other entities in your system.
fallback: Entity-Relationship (ER) diagrams are used to model the logical structure of a database by showing the relationships between different entities.

template: A Sankey diagram is fascinating for showing quantities. It would visually demonstrate how {context} moves from one state or location to another, with the width of the lines showing the volume.
fallback: Sankey diagrams are flow diagrams where the width of the arrows is proportional to the flow rate, making them great for energy or material balance.

template: An organizational chart is the way to go for {context}. It clearly defines the reporting lines and the structural hierarchy of the team.
fallback: A hierarchy diagram, such as an org chart, is used to represent a system in which units are ranked one above another.

template: If you want to show who does what, a swimlane diagram is best. It splits the flowchart into lanes, showing exactly when {context} takes over the task.
fallback: Swimlane diagrams are a specialized type of flowchart that distinguishes role responsibilities for particular steps in a process.
